societies.name: The Diamond Age (Thetes under the Feed)
societies.society: Phyleless people using public Feed-connected matter compilers

scope.period: The functioning Feed era before a hypothetical general Seed transition
scope.population: Human Thetes with practical access to public matter compilers
exclusions: All phyle members assigned identical entitlements
Drummers counted as nonworking automated components
All desired housing and services treated as free

societies.description:
Public matter compilers turn Feed inputs into basic food, water and simple goods without charging the recipient. For phyleless Thetes this creates a material floor outside ordinary wage purchase, even though their lives can remain poor and insecure. The guarantee score is moderately strong because this floor is narrow: free basic consumables do not establish access to every service, desirable home or protective community.

The ability to request output does not give Thetes effective control over its supply. Important sources and Feed infrastructure belong to powerful phyles, leaving ordinary recipients dependent on concentrated human institutions. Smaller independent Feeds qualify a picture of one universal monopoly but do not give these recipients broad productive ownership. The system is therefore placed provisionally in the concentrated-control, basic-provision regime. Human engineering, service and other work persist, and neither plentiful diamonds nor free meals determines the nonworking population share. The later Seed project remains outside this record because its decentralized potential is not an established general successor economy in the short evidence.

guarantees.basis: Free public necessities provide a narrow floor; housing, medical care and social protection are not established as universal.

control.basis: Recipients can request goods but central Feed sources and technology remain under powerful phyle control.

nonworking.basis: Selective automation and human occupational activity do not establish an all-Thete participation count.

evidence.claim: Public compilers supply basic goods freely while concentrated Feed infrastructure creates dependency.
evidence.locator: Public compiler entries; Feed-dependence discussion in Longan and Oakes

uncertainties: The guarantee is a consumables floor, not comprehensive welfare or secure housing.
Phyleless recipients are the scope; the whole planet does not receive one common economic constitution.
No precise nonworking fraction and no realized Seed outcome are inferred.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: Free public compiler output plus concentrated input control establishes a scoped basic-provision arrangement.
The Drummers perform necessary human-derived collective computation rather than replacing it with nonhuman labor.
decisions.analysis: Subsumed personality and unusual activity are not leisure. Their work developing the Seed does not establish a separate supported nonworking society.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a human-computation comparison and skip deeper reading.

decisions.reason: The Seed is an alternative under development, not a verified established society in the quick sources.
decisions.analysis: A decentralized fabrication design does not establish an actual population, access constitution or durable completed transition.
decisions.follow_up: Skip ending reconstruction; do not score technical potential as realized institutions.

decisions.reason: The short Snow Crash check does not establish automated basic provision or deliberate preservation of unnecessary jobs.
decisions.analysis: Franchise organization, virtual environments and advanced devices are insufficient admission evidence. Keyword lists are not interpreted as proof of economic absence.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; retain the unverified mechanism as an explicit gap.

decisions.reason: Active Bitworld minds are verified, but their changing support and control rules remain unresolved.
decisions.analysis: A computational afterlife can contain materially different phases and coercion. Uploading alone does not establish post-work access or justify one aggregate coordinate.

decisions.reason: Saecular consumer culture does not establish a material post-work support mechanism.
decisions.analysis: Advertising, devices and rapid cultural change are not evidence that work has ceased to govern basic distribution. Mathic institutions cannot be imported.

decisions.reason: The late orbital civilization is identifiable but its allocation system remains unclear in the quick reference.
decisions.analysis: Orbital habitability, robotics and differentiated descendants do not establish universal labor-independent necessities or one common ownership regime.
decisions.follow_up: Skip a 5000-year social reconstruction; do not use fanfiction as canonical evidence.

review_notes: Seven quick dispositions, with one record supported by clear public-compiler and Feed evidence.
Thete basic provision remains narrow. Drummers still perform human-derived work, and the Seed is not presumed to be a completed social system.
Bitworld uploading and Seveneves orbital life do not automatically establish a post-work economy.
No novel reading, paid-guide access or speculative recovery was needed.
